---
title: "Foundation 4B: Persistence modules in detail"
toc: true
---

Let $I$ be the set of filtration values under consideration, usually a finite
subset of $\mathbb R$. The symbol $\leq$ is the usual ordering of those values.
Write

$$
\mathcal K_f(a)=K_a
$$

for the complex present at value $a$. Thus $\mathcal K_f$ names the whole
filtration generated by $f$, while $K_a$ is one complex in that family. If
$a\leq b$, the filtration also contains the inclusion
$\iota_{a,b}:K_a\hookrightarrow K_b$.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Reading the notation.** Calligraphic $\mathcal K_f$ is the entire movie;
$K_a$ is one frame. The subscript $f$ records the rule that determines when
simplices enter.
:::

## From inclusions to induced maps

For $a\leq b$, the inclusion

$$
\iota_{a,b}:K_a\hookrightarrow K_b
$$

sends each simplex already present in $K_a$ to that same simplex in $K_b$.
It induces compatible maps on chain spaces and therefore a linear map on
homology:

$$
H_p(\iota_{a,b}):H_p(K_a;\mathbb F)\to H_p(K_b;\mathbb F),
\qquad [z]\mapsto[z].
$$

The same cycle $z$ may represent a non-zero class in $K_a$ and a boundary in
$K_b$ after new $(p+1)$-simplices have entered.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Intuition.** Homology converts a map between complexes into a map between
their homology spaces. Homology itself is still calculated from simplices and
boundary maps.
:::

## The functorial statement

Treat $(I,\leq)$ as a category with one arrow $a\to b$ whenever $a\leq b$.
A filtration is a functor

<span id="functor-note"></span>

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Functor.** A functor applies one rule consistently to objects and maps.
Here the filtration assigns a complex to every scale and an inclusion to every
ordered pair of scales. Homology then assigns a vector space to each complex
and a linear map to each inclusion, preserving identities and composition.
:::

$$
\mathcal K_f:(I,\leq)\to\mathbf{SimpComp}.
$$

Here $\mathbf{SimpComp}$ denotes the collection of simplicial complexes and
maps between them. The bold type indicates a category of objects and maps, not
one particular complex.

Degree-$p$ homology over a field is a functor

$$
H_p(-;\mathbb F):\mathbf{SimpComp}\to\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb F}.
$$

Here $\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb F}$ denotes vector spaces over the coefficient
field $\mathbb F$ and linear maps between them. The integer $p$ is the homology
dimension: $p=0$ tracks components, $p=1$ loops and $p=2$ cavities.

Their composition

$$
V=H_p\circ\mathcal K_f:(I,\leq)\longrightarrow\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb F}
$$

is the degree-$p$ persistence module. It assigns one homology vector space to
each filtration value and one compatible linear map to each ordered pair.
Functoriality gives the identity and composition rules automatically.

In the filtered house, let the outer edges enter at $1$, the roof-base edge at
$2$ and the roof face at $3$. At scale $2$, $H_1$ has the roof class $[r]$
and room class $[q]$. The inclusion into the scale-$3$ complex induces

$$
[r]\longmapsto 0,
\qquad
[q]\longmapsto[q].
$$

The new face makes $r$ a boundary, while $q$ remains unfilled. This is what
“apply homology to the inclusion” means: calculate how each class changes
when the same cycle is viewed in the larger complex.

For $a\leq b$,

$$
H_p^{a,b}=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H_p(K_a)\to H_p(K_b)\bigr)
$$

answers which classes present at $a$ survive until $b$. The full module
retains this information coherently for every ordered pair.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Image reminder.** The [image of a linear
map](../topic-02/algebra-survival-guide.qmd#kernel-image) consists of outputs
that actually arise. Here it contains precisely the classes at $b$ inherited
from classes already present at $a$.
:::

::: {.checkpoint-route}

You are ready to continue when you can distinguish $\iota_{a,b}$ from $H_p(\iota_{a,b})$, explain
the identity and composition laws, and read $H_p^{a,b}$ as an image.

:::
